previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, and a history of left below-knee amputation was admitted for severe right foot pain and dry gangrene. Imaging revealed subcutaneous emphysema, indicating tissue necrosis. She was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics, and after a urine culture identified Pseudomonas aeruginosa sensitive to ciprofloxacin, targeted therapy was continued. Due to extensive gangrene, she underwent a right below-knee amputation. Postoperatively, pain was initially difficult to control but improved with transition to oral morphine. Psychiatric consultation was obtained after she expressed suicidal thoughts, and citalopram was initiated for mood support. Her recovery progressed well, with stable vital signs, improving lab values, and good wound healing. She was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with a plan for ongoing antibiotic therapy, diabetes management, and multidisciplinary follow-up.

radiology_notes.text:
PICC LINE PLACEMENT

INDICATION:  IV access needed for antibiotics.

The procedure was explained to the patient.  A timeout was performed.

RADIOLOGISTS:  Dr. ___ with Dr. ___ the procedure.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the left basilic
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after
establishing intravenous access.  A peel-away sheath was then placed over a
guidewire and a double-lumen PICC line measuring 36 cm in length was then
placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in the SVC under
fluoroscopic guidance.  Position of the catheter was confirmed by a
fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided PICC 5
___ double-lumen PICC line placement via the left basilic venous approach.
Final internal length is 36 cm, with the tip positioned in SVC.  The line is
ready to use.
